subject: Mathematics
statusNote: Rebuilt on 9 November 2026 from the official Pearson 4MA1 specification PDF (Issue 2), read as raw text: papers, durations, marks, weights, tiers, calculator rules, assessment objective weightings and every Foundation and Higher content statement. Pupils sit 4MA1, so the course is now taught from 4MA1 itself (it was previously taught from the UK GCSE 1MA1 with a 4MA1 exam entry). Units are the 32 Higher units of Pearson's two-year 4MA1 scheme of work, the school's KS4 maths scheme (a generic Pearson document), placed in the scheme's suggested Higher order over five terms with the sixth for revision. Each point is paraphrased with its 4MA1 reference; Higher assumes the Foundation content, so Foundation references are included. Series: January and June.

sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) specification, Issue 2 (November 2017)
Pearson: information for centres entering private candidates

tiers: Foundation (Papers 1F and 2F, grades 5 to 1) or Higher (Papers 1H and 2H, grades 9 to 4, with grade 3 allowed). The school teaches the Higher tier; Higher questions assume Foundation content.

assessment.title: Higher tier paper 1
assessment.content: All Higher content, assuming the Foundation content: number, algebra, sequences, functions and graphs, geometry, vectors, statistics and probability
assessment.format: Written paper set and marked by Pearson; calculator allowed; Higher formulae sheet supplied; about 40% of marks at grades 4 and 5.

assessment.title: Higher tier paper 2
assessment.content: All Higher content, assuming the Foundation content
assessment.format: Written paper set and marked by Pearson; calculator allowed; Higher formulae sheet supplied; instruments and tracing paper may be used.

nonExam: None. Two externally assessed written papers only.

aos.desc: Number and algebra: numbers, calculations, numerical problems, equations, formulae, identities, sequences, functions and graphs.
Shape, space and measures: geometry, trigonometry, vectors and transformation geometry.

commandWords.meaning: Find a numerical answer, showing the method.
Give enough working to reach a stated answer convincingly.
Give a logical argument, with justified steps, that a result is always true (Higher).
State why, using mathematical language or a rule.
Find the value or values of the unknown that satisfy the equation.
Rewrite an expression in the required algebraic form.
Use rounded values to find an approximate answer.
Show the key features of a graph or shape, with accuracy as the question requires.

skills: Efficient calculator use in both papers, checking results by estimation.
Problem solving (about 30% of Higher marks) and mathematical reasoning (about 20%): chains of reasoning, arguments and proofs.
Setting out working so method marks can be awarded.
Using the Higher formulae sheet and recalling formulae it does not give.
Geometry equipment: ruler, protractor and compasses for constructions and bearings.

links.how: Maths supplies substitution, rearrangement and standard form; Science applies them to equations such as speed, density and pressure.

links.topic: Speed, density and pressure as compound units
links.how: Maths develops compound measures and proportion; Physics uses them in motion and materials questions.
Maths teaches gradient and area under a graph; Physics interprets them as speed, acceleration and distance.

links.topic: Ratios, percentages and unit conversion in calculations
links.how: Maths builds proportional reasoning; Chemistry uses it for concentrations, reacting quantities and percentage yield.
Maths teaches averages and spread; Biology applies them to sampled data such as quadrat counts.
Maths defines rules for sequences and functions; Computing expresses them as algorithms, loops and subprograms.

links.topic: Powers of 2, standard form and approximation
links.how: Maths supplies indices and standard form; Computing uses powers of 2 for binary, storage sizes and overflow.
Maths defines functions, composite and inverse functions; Computing expresses the same mappings as subprograms with inputs and outputs.

links.topic: Scale, map work and data handling
links.how: Maths teaches scale factors and bearings; Geography uses them on maps and in analysing fieldwork data.
